mainTopic: Knowledge and liability for a חטאת: ספק ידיעה in טומאת מקדש, and a sinner who does not know which sin he did
overview: The amud finishes a ברייתא about a person who walked on one of two paths, one טמא and one טהור, and then entered the מקדש. רבא explains that רבי שמעון's exemption even in the first case is about מקצת ידיעה, partial knowledge. In the case where he became pure in between, the גמרא asks why he is liable without real ידיעה. ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require ידיעה בתחלה. רבי יוחנן says that even the רבנן agree, because for טומאה, ספק ידיעה counts as ידיעה. The גמרא settles the apparent contradictions in both sages: רבי יוחנן's rule applies only to טומאה because of the wording 'ונעלם ממנו', and ריש לקיש chose רבי ישמעאל to teach that רבי ישמעאל rejects ידיעה בתחלה completely. A new משנה then brings cases where a person surely sinned but does not know which sin he did. רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts, and several תנאים limit where this argument applies. The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's 'מה נפשך' reasoning and רבי יהושע's proof from 'אשר חטא בה'. רבי אליעזר uses that word only to exclude a מתעסק.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's opinion and רבי שמעון בן יהודה's report
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: רבי שמעון exempts in the case where he became pure in between, and רבי שמעון בן יהודה reports that רבי שמעון exempts in all the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון exempts in this case. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says, in רבי שמעון's name, that he exempts in all of the cases.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the ברייתא about the two paths. Two versions of רבי שמעון's opinion are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case right before this, he entered after the first path, became pure, then entered again after the second path. רבי שמעון exempts him there, because at no single moment did he know for sure that he was טמא. רבי שמעון בן יהודה goes further and says רבי שמעון exempts in every case of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts (here, from bringing a קרבן)
In this one (the case just mentioned)
In all of them (every case in the ברייתא)
In the name of

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts in this case.
phrases.notes: "This case" is the one right before it in the ברייתא: he entered, became pure through sprinkling and immersion, then walked the second path and entered.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר בְּכוּלָּן
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda exempts in all of them
in the name of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון exempts when he became pure in between. According to רבי שמעון בן יהודה, רבי שמעון exempts in all the cases.

steps.title: Even in the first case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן יהודה's version: how can רבי שמעון exempt even in the first case, where he clearly knew he was טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does he exempt even in the first case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the word "all" in רבי שמעון בן יהודה's report. It sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case he walked both paths before entering, so he must have touched the טמא one. That is certain knowledge of טומאה, so there seems to be no reason to exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one (the first case of the ברייתא)
And even

phrases.english: And even in the first case?
phrases.notes: The first case: he walked both paths and only then entered the מקדש, so he surely knew he was טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the word בכולן in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יהודה's claim that רבי שמעון exempts in all the cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the first case he had certain knowledge of his טומאה, so he should be liable.

steps.title: רבא: he forgot the first path
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the first case is about someone who forgot the first path while walking the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What case are we dealing with? Where he walked on the first path, and while walking on the second he forgot that he had walked on the first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by describing the case more narrowly. Here the person's knowledge was not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he forgot the first path while on the second, he never had both facts in mind at once. So his knowledge that he was definitely טמא is only partial, and that gives רבי שמעון room to exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a phrase used to narrow the case)
He forgot
His walking

phrases.english: Rava said:
What are we dealing with here?
Such as where he walked on the first path
and at the time he was walking on the second
he forgot that he had walked on the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the first case meant he knowingly walked both paths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where he forgot the first path while walking the second, so his knowledge was incomplete.

steps.title: The dispute: does partial knowledge count?
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the argument: the תנא קמא holds מקצת ידיעה counts as ידיעה, and רבי שמעון holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they argue about: the תנא קמא holds that partial knowledge is like knowledge, and רבי שמעון holds that partial knowledge is not like knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by naming the exact point of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He knew about each path, but not both together. The תנא קמא says that partial knowledge is enough to make him liable. רבי שמעון says it is not enough, so he is exempt even in the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
The first (unnamed) opinion in the ברייתא
Partial knowledge
Is considered like, resembles

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון is whether מקצת ידיעה counts as real ידיעה for liability.

phrases.english: And about this they disagree:
The first Tanna holds:
partial knowledge is considered like knowledge,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
partial knowledge is not considered like knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by stating the principle behind the argument.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether מקצת ידיעה counts as ידיעה.

steps.title: Back to the middle case: pure in between, still liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the ברייתא's case where he entered, became pure, walked the second path and entered again, and is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If he walked on the first path and entered, was sprinkled and immersed, then walked on the second path and entered, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא so it can question it. This step sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between the two entries he became fully טהור. So at each entry he was only possibly טמא, yet the ברייתא (the תנא קמא) still makes him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Entered (the מקדש)
Was sprinkled (with the ashes of the פרה אדומה)
Immersed (in a מקוה)
Liable (to bring a קרבן)

phrases.english: The Master said:
If he walked on the first path and entered,
and was sprinkled and immersed,
and walked on the second and entered, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's point and returns to an earlier line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who entered after each path, with purification in between, is liable according to the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Why liable without knowledge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how he can be liable when he never had definite knowledge of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he liable? He never had knowledge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן for entering the מקדש while טמא normally needs ידיעה, real knowledge of being טמא. Here, because he became pure in between, there was never a moment when he knew for sure that he was טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Knowledge (awareness of being טמא, needed for liability)

phrases.english: Why is he liable?
But he did not have knowledge!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי חַיָּיב? הָא לָא הֲוַי לֵיהּ יְדִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that he is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability needs definite ידיעה, and here there never was any.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: this follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require ידיעה at the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Whose view is this? It is רבי ישמעאל's, who does not require knowledge at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש solves the question by saying which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no ידיעה is needed before the sin, then the missing knowledge here is no problem. He is liable even though he never knew for sure he was טמא at the time.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Does not require
At the beginning (before the sin)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yishmael's,
who does not require knowledge at the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ruling follows the usual view that requires ידיעה at the beginning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require ידיעה בתחילה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even the רבנן, since doubtful knowledge counted here
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא can follow the רבנן too, because in this case ספק ידיעה was treated like ידיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it follows the רבנן. Here they treated doubtful knowledge like knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer that does not need רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do require ידיעה. But in this case they counted uncertain knowledge (he knew he might be טמא) as enough. So the ruling fits their view as well.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
The Rabbis (the majority view, which requires ידיעה)
Doubtful or uncertain knowledge

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to why he is liable without clear knowledge: ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל (no ידיעה needed at the beginning). רבי יוחנן says it even fits the רבנן, who here count ספק ידיעה as ידיעה.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two answers set up the contradictions between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that the גמרא wants to explain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis;
here they treated doubtful knowledge like knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the challenge of step 6, in place of ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the רבנן could not hold him liable without definite knowledge.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן agree, because here ספק ידיעה counts as ידיעה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן's rule that ספק ידיעה counts as ידיעה applies to the whole Torah, it clashes with his own earlier statement about ספק ידיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think רבי יוחנן meant: here they treated doubtful knowledge like knowledge, and the same is true for the whole Torah. If so, רבי יוחנן contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between רבי יוחנן's answer in step 8 and something רבי יוחנן said earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רבי יוחנן said that in our case ספק ידיעה was treated like full ידיעה. Earlier, he had said that ספק ידיעה is not like ידיעה, so it does not split sins into separate חטאות. If his new rule applies everywhere, the two statements clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind (you might think)
Here they made it so (here they treated ספק ידיעה like ידיעה)
The same law applies
A contradiction between two statements of the same sage

phrases.english: It enters your mind: here they made it so,
phrases.notes: "Here they made it so" is רבי יוחנן's line from the previous step: here ספק ידיעה was treated like real knowledge.

phrases.english: and the same applies to the entire Torah,
then Rabbi Yochanan is difficult against Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: Earlier רבי יוחנן said doubtful knowledge does not divide sins into separate offerings, so it is not like real knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: סלקא דעתך: כאן עשו, והוא הדין לכל התורה כולה, קשיא דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of רבי יוחנן from step 8 by setting it against his earlier statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that ספק ידיעה was treated like ידיעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ספק ידיעה is like ידיעה everywhere, it should also divide sins into separate חטאות, which רבי יוחנן earlier denied.

steps.title: ריש לקיש seems to contradict himself too
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's answer that the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל seems to clash with his earlier statement about רבי's view on ספק ידיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second contradiction, this time between ריש לקיש's answer in step 7 and his earlier statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ריש לקיש said that according to רבי, ספק ידיעה divides sins into separate חטאות, so it works like real knowledge. If so, he could have explained the ברייתא that way. Instead, in step 7 he needed to say the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Divides sins, so each one needs its own חטאת
Sin offering brought for an accidental sin

phrases.english: Reish Lakish is difficult against Reish Lakish.
phrases.notes: Earlier ריש לקיש said that for רבי, doubtful knowledge does divide sins, yet here he reached all the way to רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel contradiction, now about ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation in step 7 that the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש himself said earlier that according to רבי, ספק ידיעה acts like ידיעה (it divides sins into separate חטאות). So he could have explained the liability by following רבי, and did not need to go to רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule applies only here
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction in רבי יוחנן is solved: ספק ידיעה counts as ידיעה only in this case of טומאה, not in the rest of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבי יוחנן against רבי יוחנן is not a problem: here they treated it like knowledge, but in the whole Torah, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction by limiting רבי יוחנן's rule to this case only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that 'it applies to the whole Torah' from step 9 is rejected. In this case of טומאה, ספק ידיעה is treated like ידיעה, but everywhere else it is not, so his earlier statement still stands. The word בשלמא hints that the ריש לקיש contradiction is not solved yet. Steps 13-14 deal with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted (this one is fine, but the other is still a problem)
It is not difficult
The entire Torah, all other sins

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Yochanan against Rabbi Yochanan
is not difficult: here they made it so,
but in the entire Torah, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלמא דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן לא קשיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule that ספק ידיעה counts as ידיעה applies to the whole Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to this case of טומאה; in the rest of the Torah ספק ידיעה is not like ידיעה.

steps.title: Why טומאה is different: the wording of the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about טומאה makes one liable even with doubtful knowledge, while the general פסוק about sins requires real knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Here, about טומאה, it is written: 'and it was hidden from him, and he is impure'. The פסוק makes him liable even with knowledge that has doubt in it. But about the whole Torah it is written: 'or his sin is made known to him', so only if he has knowledge is he liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for why טומאה is an exception: two different פסוקים use different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about טומאה speaks of something 'hidden from him', and the גמרא reads this as including knowledge that has doubt in it. The general פסוק says 'his sin is made known to him', which requires real knowledge. So רבי יוחנן's two statements fit two different areas of law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Regarding impurity (entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא)
And it was hidden from him (the טומאה פסוק)
His sin is made known to him (the general פסוק)
The פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו does ספק ידיעה count as ידיעה, because of the wording 'ונעלם ממנו'. For the rest of the Torah, 'או הודע אליו' requires real knowledge.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the requirement of ידיעה can work differently in different areas, depending on how each פסוק is worded.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Here, regarding impurity, it is written:
"and it was hidden from him, and he is impure"
even knowledge that has doubt in it,
the verse makes him liable,
but regarding the entire Torah it is written:
"or his sin is made known to him"

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לֵיהּ יְדִיעָה הוּא דְּמִחַיַּיב.
phrases.english: only if he has knowledge is he liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי טעמא? הכא, גבי טומאה כתיב: ונעלם ממנו והוא טמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from the פסוקים for the limit set in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source from the פסוקים: different wording in different areas
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no reason to treat טומאה differently from the rest of the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טומאה פסוק ('ונעלם ממנו') includes doubtful knowledge, while the general פסוק ('או הודע אליו') requires real knowledge.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש place the ברייתא with רבי?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the problem with רבי יוחנן is solved, the problem with ריש לקיש is still standing. Why did he place the ברייתא with רבי ישמעאל, when he could have placed it with רבי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for ריש לקיש there is still a difficulty. Instead of saying the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, he should say it follows רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the challenge against ריש לקיש from Step 10. That challenge has not been answered yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's contradiction was solved in Steps 11-12. ריש לקיש's own earlier statement about רבי's view on ספק ידיעה shows that רבי's view would fit the ברייתא. So why did he reach for רבי ישמעאל instead?

keyTerms.meaning: a difficulty that still has no answer
instead of setting it (the ברייתא) according to
let him set it according to

phrases.english: But for ריש לקיש it is difficult
instead of establishing it like רבי ישמעאל
let him establish it like רבי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the open challenge against ריש לקיש after the challenge against רבי יוחנן was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's choice to place the ברייתא with רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's own statement about רבי already gives a ready match for the ברייתא, so it seems unnecessary to name רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: He wanted to teach about רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש chose רבי ישמעאל on purpose. He wanted to teach that רבי ישמעאל also does not require knowing about the sin beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is teaching us: רבי ישמעאל also does not require ידיעה בתחלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש picked רבי ישמעאל to teach us something new about רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing the ברייתא with רבי would have been easy. Placing it with רבי ישמעאל adds new information: he too does not need the person to know about the טומאה before the sin in order to obligate a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he is teaching us
awareness at the start, before the sin happened by mistake

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us
that רבי ישמעאל too
does not require knowledge at the beginning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Purpose of the statement: the unusual choice was made in order to teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming רבי ישמעאל was pointless, since רבי already fit
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that רבי ישמעאל also does not require ידיעה בתחלה

steps.title: A משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we already know this from a משנה. There רבי ישמעאל uses the words 'ונעלם ממנו' for something else, so clearly he does not learn ידיעה בתחלה from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is already a משנה! We learned: רבי ישמעאל says, 'ונעלם ממנו' is written two times. This makes a person liable for forgetting the טומאה and for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 14. Why would ריש לקיש need to teach something a משנה already shows?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requirement of ידיעה בתחלה comes from the extra 'ונעלם ממנו'. רבי ישמעאל uses both mentions for other teachings: forgetting that he was טמא, and forgetting that the place was the מקדש. So he obviously has no source for ידיעה בתחלה, and ריש לקיש's lesson seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: but this is already taught in a משנה
'and it was hidden from him', the words of the פסוק
forgetting that he was טמא
forgetting that the place was the מקדש

phrases.english: But this is a משנה!
As we learned: רבי ישמעאל says
'And it was hidden from him' is written twice
to make him liable for forgetting the impurity
and for forgetting the Temple!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 as unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ריש לקיש was teaching something new about רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל uses up the פסוק for other teachings, so a משנה already shows he has no source for ידיעה בתחלה.

steps.title: Maybe he had a tradition instead of a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: It was still necessary to say it. We might have thought that רבי ישמעאל has no פסוק for ידיעה בתחלה but holds it from a tradition. ריש לקיש teaches that he does not hold it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: he has no פסוק for it, but he has it from a tradition. So he teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש's lesson is still needed even though the משנה exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only proves that רבי ישמעאל does not learn ידיעה בתחלה from the פסוק. It does not prove he rejects the rule. He could still hold it from a tradition. ריש לקיש's placing of the ברייתא shows that he does not require it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed
you might have thought
a פסוק as the source
a tradition that was passed down

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש places the ברייתא with רבי ישמעאל to show that רבי ישמעאל rejects ידיעה בתחלה completely, not just that he lacks a פסוק for it.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גמרא' does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition received from teachers.

phrases.english: It was necessary
it would enter your mind to say
he does not have it from a verse
but he has it from a tradition
so he teaches us otherwise

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the lesson is needed: it rules out a possible wrong assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל has no פסוק for ידיעה בתחלה, but he holds it from a tradition
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל does not require ידיעה בתחלה at all

steps.title: New משנה: he sinned but doesn't know which sin
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה brings three cases. In each one a person surely did one of two sins by mistake, but he does not know which one. רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: חלב and נותר were in front of him. He ate one of them and does not know which. His wife who was a נדה and his sister were with him in the house. He sinned by mistake with one of them and does not know with which. שבת and יום הכיפורים came one after the other, and he did מלאכה during בין השמשות and does not know on which day. רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It presents a disagreement about a person who surely sinned but does not know which sin it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case, both choices are sins that carry a חטאת, so a sin surely happened. The only question is whether not knowing exactly which sin he did stops him from bringing a חטאת. רבי אליעזר obligates him, and רבי יהושע exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden fat of an animal
meat of a קרבן left over past its time
a woman in her time of menstrual impurity
twilight, which might belong to either day
a sin offering brought for a mistaken sin
exempts

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת opens the next part of the sugya: does a person need to know exactly which sin he did in order to bring a חטאת?

phrases.english: MISHNA
Forbidden fat and leftover sacrificial meat were before him
and he ate one of them
and he does not know which of them he ate
his menstruating wife and his sister were with him in the house
he sinned by mistake with one of them
phrases.notes: He means he was with one of them as husband and wife, by mistake.

phrases.english: and he does not know with which of them he sinned
Shabbat and Yom Kippur
phrases.notes: The two days fell right next to each other, so the twilight between them could belong to either one.

phrases.english: and he did forbidden work at twilight
and he does not know on which of them he did it
Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin offering
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a person surely did one of two sins that each carry a חטאת but does not know which, רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.

steps.title: No argument about work done at twilight
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that work done at twilight is exempt, because part of it was done on one day and part on the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: They did not argue about someone who did work at twilight. Everyone agrees he is exempt, because part of the work was done on one day and part on the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי narrows the argument from the last step. He takes the twilight case out of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At twilight, the work is split between two days, so no single holy day has a full act of work done on it. Because of that, the person is not obligated at all, and there is nothing to argue about. That leaves only the other cases for the real argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the in-between time when it is unclear if it is still day or already night
They did not disagree
Exempt, not obligated
A forbidden kind of work

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
They did not disagree about one who does forbidden work
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע from the last step.

phrases.english: at twilight, that he is exempt,
phrases.notes: This is the case where שבת and יום כיפור fall right next to each other, so twilight joins the two days.

phrases.english: because I say:
he did part of it today
and he did part of it the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the argument from Step 17 by taking out the twilight case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work done at twilight is exempt according to everyone, because it is split between two days.

steps.title: Where the argument really is
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the argument is about work done in the middle of a day when the person does not know if it was שבת or יום כיפור, or does not know which kind of work he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did they argue about? About someone who did work in the middle of the day and does not know if it was on שבת or on יום כיפור. Or about someone who did work and does not know which kind of work it was. In those cases רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי finishes his statement. He tells us exactly which cases the argument is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the person surely did a full sin on a full day. The only thing missing is that he does not know exactly which sin it was. רבי אליעזר says a sure sin is enough for a חטאת, and רבי יהושע says he must know what the sin was.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligates
In the middle of the day (not at twilight)
Which kind of work

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, the argument is only when a full sin was surely done but the person does not know which one it was.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About one who does work in the middle of the day
and does not know whether he did it on Shabbat
or whether he did it on Yom Kippur,
or about one who does work and does not know
which kind of work he did.
For Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוסי's statement by naming the cases where they do argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They argue when work was surely done on a full day but the person does not know which day or which kind of work.

steps.title: Exempt even from an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that רבי יהושע exempts the person even from an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: רבי יהושע would exempt him even from an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds to רבי יהושע's view. He says the person brings no חטאת and also no אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that if רבי יהושע exempts from a חטאת, the person should at least bring an אשם תלוי. רבי יהודה says no. In רבי יהושע's view, he brings no offering at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is not sure if he sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two offerings. A חטאת is for a sin a person knows he did. An אשם תלוי is for a case of doubt. רבי יהודה says רבי יהושע exempts from both.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Rabbi Yehoshua would exempt him
even from a provisional guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: פּוֹטְרוֹ הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how far רבי יהושע's exemption reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, the person brings neither a חטאת nor an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: Only two categories bring the argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון and רבי שמעון שזורי say that when the doubt is inside one category, everyone obligates. The argument is only when the doubt is between two categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון and רבי שמעון שזורי say: They did not argue about a case of one category, where everyone agrees he is liable. What did they argue about? About a case of two categories. There רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more תנאים give their own way of drawing the line of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person knows what kind of sin he did and is only unsure about some detail, everyone agrees he brings a חטאת. Only when he does not know which of two kinds of sin he did does רבי יהושע exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: One category or type of sin
Two different categories of sin
Liable, obligated

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Shimon Shezuri say:
They did not disagree about a case
that is of one category, that he is liable,
phrases.notes: For example, he picked a grape on שבת and only does not know which vine it came from.

phrases.english: about what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת,
phrases.english: about a case that involves two categories,
phrases.notes: For example, he does not know if he picked from a vine or from a fig tree.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמְרִים: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way from רבי יוסי's to define the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt inside one category is liable according to everyone. They argue only about a doubt between two categories.

steps.title: Meant to pick one fruit and picked another
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says they argue even when a person meant to pick one fruit on שבת and picked a different one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Even if he meant to pick figs and picked grapes, or grapes and picked figs, or black ones and picked white ones, or white ones and picked black ones, רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה stretches the argument to a new case. Here the person knows what he did, but he did something different from what he meant to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is wider than the ones before. Here there is no doubt about what was done, only a gap between what he planned and what actually happened. רבי יהודה says the same argument applies here too.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended, he meant to
He picked, he gathered
Figs
Grapes

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Even if he meant to pick figs
and picked grapes,
or meant to pick grapes and picked figs,
or black ones and picked white ones,
or white ones and picked black ones –
Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּוֵּון לִלְקוֹט תְּאֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the argument to a case of doing something different from what was planned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They argue even when a person meant to pick one fruit and picked another.

steps.title: Does רבי יהושע really exempt here?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה wonders whether רבי יהושע really exempts in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: I wonder if רבי יהושע really exempts in this case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה raises a doubt about the case he just gave. He finds it hard to believe that רבי יהושע would exempt here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the person did mean to do a forbidden act of picking on שבת. He just picked a different fruit. So it is hard to see why רבי יהושע would exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: I wonder, I am surprised

phrases.aramaic: תְּמֵיהַנִי אִם פָּטַר בָּהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: I wonder if Rabbi Yehoshua exempted in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּמֵיהַנִי אִם פָּטַר בָּהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the case from Step 22 really fits רבי יהושע's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהושע exempts one who meant to pick figs and picked grapes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The person did mean to do forbidden work on שבת, so it is hard to see a reason to exempt him.

steps.title: Then what does 'אשר חטא בה' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: if he is not exempt, what does the פסוק 'אשר חטא בה' come to exclude?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the תורה say 'אשר חטא בה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה challenges רבי יהודה's surprise. If the person is liable, the words of the פסוק seem to have no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשר חטא בה' sound like they limit when a person brings a חטאת. If even someone who picked the wrong fruit brings one, we need to know what these words leave out.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
'In which he sinned,' words from the פסוק about a חטאת

phrases.english: If so,
why is it said: "in which he sinned"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's surprise from Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the person who picked the wrong fruit is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'אשר חטא בה' must be leaving something out. If this case is liable, what is left out?

steps.title: It excludes a מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק comes to exclude a מתעסק, someone who did not mean to do a forbidden act at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question. The פסוק still has a job: it leaves out someone who did not mean to do any forbidden act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is different from the fruit picker. The fruit picker meant to do a forbidden act and only got the object wrong. A מתעסק never meant to do a forbidden act at all, and that is who the פסוק exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out
Someone who acts without meaning to do a forbidden act at all

steps.whatToRemember: There are two different cases. Someone who meant to do a forbidden act but got the object wrong may be liable even according to רבי יהושע, as רבי יהודה suspects. A מתעסק, who never meant to do a forbidden act, is exempt because of the פסוק 'אשר חטא בה'.

phrases.english: To exclude one who acts unawares.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24 by giving the פסוק a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a different case to exclude.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'אשר חטא בה' must exclude the person who picked the wrong fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אשר חטא בה' excludes only a מתעסק, who never meant to do a forbidden act. So the fruit picker can still be liable.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Either way he sinned, so he is liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's reasoning. Whichever of the two forbidden things the person did, he is חייב, so he must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר said: Whichever way you look at it, he is liable. If he ate חלב, he is liable. If he ate נותר, he is liable. If he was with his wife who was a נדה, he is liable. If he was with his sister, he is liable. If he did מלאכה on שבת, he is liable. If he did מלאכה on יום הכיפורים, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that gives the reason behind רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה. He says the person must bring a חטאת no matter which sin he actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, both options are real sins that carry a חטאת. So the doubt is only about which sin he did, not about whether he sinned. For רבי אליעזר, that is enough to make him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it. Every possible option leads to the same result.
Forbidden fats of an animal
Leftover meat of a קרבן, eaten after its time ran out
A woman in her time of menstrual impurity
Liable. Here it means he must bring a חטאת.

steps.whyThisMatters: This מה נפשך logic is the whole basis of רבי אליעזר's side of the argument. Everything that follows in the sugya is a response to it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer said: Whichever way you look at it,
if it was forbidden fat that he ate, he is liable;
if it was notar that he ate, he is liable!
if it was his menstruating wife he had relations with, he is liable;
if it was his sister he had relations with, he is liable!
if it was on Shabbat that he did labor, he is liable;

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עָשָׂה מְלָאכָה – חַיָּיב!
phrases.english: if it was on Yom Kippur that he did labor, he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the first case in the משנה, the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both options are sins that carry a חטאת, the person is חייב even though he does not know which one he did.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: He must know which sin he did
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the מה נפשך logic. The פסוק ״אשר חטא בה״ requires the person to know exactly which sin he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: The פסוק says ״אשר חטא בה״, "in which he sinned." This teaches that he is not liable until he knows exactly what he sinned with.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers רבי אליעזר with a פסוק. He shows that knowing "I sinned somehow" is not enough to bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״בה״ ("in it") points to one specific sin. So the תורה asks for knowledge of the exact sin, not just general knowledge that some sin happened. This blocks רבי אליעזר's "either way" reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: "In which he sinned": the words of the פסוק about bringing a חטאת
Until it becomes known to him
With what he sinned, meaning the specific sin

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
It says: "In which he sinned" —
meaning, not until it becomes known to him with what he sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רבי אליעזר's מה נפשך reasoning from Step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that general knowledge of having sinned is enough to obligate a חטאת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק ״בה״ requires knowing the specific sin, so the 'either way' logic does not work.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר do with the word 'in it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר reads the word ״בה״, since he does not use it the way רבי יהושע does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with this word ״בה״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. The words of a פסוק are never extra, so if רבי אליעזר does not learn רבי יהושע's rule from ״בה״, what does he learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that every word in the תורה teaches something. רבי אליעזר rejects רבי יהושע's reading, so he must use ״בה״ for something else. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? How does he use this word or פסוק?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
what does he do with this word "in it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הַאי ״בָּהּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יהושע's proof from ״בה״, the גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר explains that same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי אליעזר learns from the word ״בה״.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר uses the word to exclude a מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר needs ״בה״ to teach that a מתעסק, someone who did not mean to do the act at all, is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to exclude a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר uses ״בה״ for a different lesson: a מתעסק is not חייב a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, ״בה״ means the person must have meant to do this act, even if he did not know it was forbidden. A מתעסק did not mean to do the act, so he is excluded. Since the word is used up for this lesson, it does not teach רבי יהושע's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for something else, another lesson
To exclude; it comes to leave out a case
Someone who did an act without meaning to do it at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: if both options are sins with a חטאת, he is חייב either way. רבי יהושע: ״אשר חטא בה״ means he must know the exact sin. רבי אליעזר uses ״בה״ only to exclude a מתעסק.
steps.confusionAlert: A מתעסק is different from a regular שוגג. A שוגג meant to do the act but did not know it was forbidden, and he does bring a חטאת. A מתעסק did not mean to do the act at all.

phrases.english: He needs it
